_meta.description: Canonical ordered pipeline steps for spatial / single-cell analysis. 'order' fixes the sequence; inclusion of each step is decided by the recommender from platform + goals + experiment type.

steps.name: Data loading & representation
steps.purpose: Read raw platform output into a common in-memory representation (AnnData / SpatialData) so every downstream tool interoperates.

steps.name: Quality control & filtering
steps.purpose: Remove low-quality cells/spots/bins and low-count genes; for imaging, filter by transcripts-per-cell, cell area, and negative-probe rate.
steps.expert_note: QC thresholds are tissue- and platform-specific. There is no universal cutoff; inspect distributions before choosing.

steps.name: Cell segmentation
steps.purpose: Assign transcripts/signal to individual cells. Required for imaging-based and high-resolution binned platforms; not applicable to multi-cell Visium spots.
steps.expert_note: UNSOLVED in the general case. Segmentation is the single largest source of error in imaging-based spatial data and every downstream count depends on it. Always visually QC boundaries; no tool is reliable across all tissues.

steps.name: Normalization & feature selection
steps.purpose: Correct for sequencing depth / total-count differences and select informative genes.

steps.name: Batch correction / integration
steps.purpose: Remove technical variation between sections, samples, donors, or runs while (ideally) preserving biology, producing a shared embedding.
steps.expert_note: NOT SOLVED reliably. Every method can over-correct (erase real biological differences) or under-correct. Always sanity-check with known markers and by confirming that expected biological differences survive. This is especially dangerous in disease-vs-control designs where the effect you care about can be 'corrected' away.

steps.name: Spatial alignment / 3D reconstruction
steps.purpose: Register serial sections into a common coordinate framework (2D pairwise alignment or full 3D stack reconstruction).
steps.expert_note: Hard and imperfect. Section-to-section distortion, tears, folds, and unknown z-spacing all degrade results. Alignment quality must be inspected visually; quantitative scores can look fine while anatomy is wrong.

steps.name: Dimensionality reduction & clustering
steps.purpose: PCA/latent embedding + neighbors graph + Leiden/Louvain clustering to define transcriptional groups prior to annotation.

steps.name: Cell type annotation
steps.purpose: Assign biological cell-type labels to single cells (imaging / HD) via reference mapping or marker-based manual annotation.
steps.expert_note: Automated labels are a starting point, not ground truth. References rarely match your exact tissue/condition; marker-based confirmation and expert review are mandatory. Ambiguous or novel states will be mislabeled.

steps.name: Spot deconvolution
steps.purpose: For multi-cell spots (Visium) or coarse bins: estimate cell-type proportions per spot using a matched single-cell reference.
steps.expert_note: Results are only as good as the single-cell reference. A missing or mismatched cell type in the reference produces confident but wrong proportions. Validate against known anatomy.

steps.name: Spatial domain identification
steps.purpose: Cluster cells/spots using expression AND spatial position into coherent tissue domains / niches.
steps.expert_note: The number of domains is a user choice with no objective ground truth; different tools/resolutions give different domains. Interpret anatomically.

steps.name: Spatially variable genes & differential expression
steps.purpose: Identify genes that vary across space (SVG) and genes differentially expressed between conditions, domains, or cell types.
steps.expert_note: Spot-level DE is confounded by cell-type composition. For condition comparisons, pseudobulk per sample (not per cell/spot) to avoid pseudo-replication and false positives.

steps.name: Cell-cell communication / niche analysis
steps.purpose: Infer ligand-receptor interactions and neighborhood/niche structure from spatial proximity.
steps.expert_note: Ligand-receptor inference is correlational and reference-database-dependent; spatial proximity does not prove signaling. Treat outputs as hypotheses.

steps.name: Visualization & reporting
steps.purpose: Interactive and publication-quality spatial visualization, including 3D viewing of reconstructed stacks.
